# Sprint 1 Review Feedback

**Reviewer:** Senior Tech Lead Reviewer Agent
**Date:** 2026-10-20
**Sprint Reference:** grimoires/loa/sprint.md
**Implementation Report:** grimoires/loa/a2a/sprint-1/reviewer.md (carries pr/PR.md; no `## AC Verification` section)

---

## Overall Assessment

The change under review is `pr/head.diff`: the `/chart` decision-map workflow (four new scripts, a skill, a command, a research agent), `map` and `spike` artifact types in `validate-artifact.sh`, the SP-1 spike fence and the D-5.9 spike-delete predicate in `block-destructive-bash.sh`, spike handling in `run-mode-ice.sh`, the question-bead lints on the build path, the `charting` planning phase in `golden-path.sh`, and ten bats suites. The shell work is careful: write order and idempotency in `chart-ticket.sh` hold as documented, the unblock probe cleans its worktree on every path, the frontier re-filters `br ready` output, and the fence corpus rows for SP-1 all pass.

I ran the ten touched suites against an overlay of the repository with the PR applied (`pr/head/` over the workspace, executable bits restored). Results:

| Suite | Result |
|---|---|
| charting-decisions | 28/29 — CD-10 fails on head (finding 2) |
| chart-frontier, charting-lint, golden-path-charting, run-mode-ice, unattended-prototype, agents-md-gen | all pass |
| spike-validator | 13/16 — "unparsable ledger keeps the block" fails on head (finding 1); two need `grimoires/loa/spikes/TEMPLATE.md`, absent in this workspace |
| validate-artifact | 48/60 — the 12 failures need the live ledger, absent in this workspace (pre-existing tests) |
| skill-capabilities | 33/36 — the 3 failures are the installed yq (4.40, no `tostring`), pre-existing tests |

Two defects introduced by the PR are reproduced and each is caught by a test the PR itself ships, so the change cannot merge as is. The `reviewer.md` carries only the PR title; there is no `## AC Verification` walkthrough, which is itself an automatic CHANGES_REQUIRED under this skill. Phase 2.5 (adversarial cross-model review) did not run: `.loa.config.yaml` sets `flatline_protocol.code_review.enabled: false`.

**Verdict:** CHANGES REQUIRED

---

## Changes Required

### 1. Safety fence: an unparsable ledger opens the spike-delete gate

- **HIGH** (confidence: high) `head/.claude/hooks/safety/block-destructive-bash.sh:651` — `_fr11_spike_decided` pipes `yq -o=json` into `jq -e`; the hook has no pipefail by design (line 14), so when yq fails to parse `grimoires/loa/decisions.yaml` it prints nothing and jq 1.6 exits 0 on empty input. The predicate then reports "decided" and `git branch -D spike/<slug>` on an unmerged spike branch is allowed.
**File:** `head/.claude/hooks/safety/block-destructive-bash.sh:651`
**Issue:** Reproduced in a scratch repo with `decisions: [unclosed` as the ledger: the hook exits 0 (allow). With no ledger file it blocks (FR-1.1), with a decided row it allows, so the gap is exactly the parse-failure path. The PR's own test "D-5.9: an unparsable ledger keeps the block" (`head/tests/unit/spike-validator.bats:262-269`) fails on head.
**Why This Matters:** The comment at line 641 promises "any failed lookup keeps the block". A corrupted or half-written ledger (the writer uses temp-and-rename, but a hand edit or merge conflict does not) silently turns a fail-closed fence into fail-open, and the lost work is the unmerged prototype the branch exists to preserve.
**Required Fix:** Capture the yq output first and fail closed when it is empty or yq returned non-zero, and do not rely on `jq -e` with possibly empty input:
```bash
local j
j=$(yq -o=json -I0 '.' "$ledger" 2>/dev/null) || return 1
[[ -n "$j" ]] || return 1
[[ "$(printf '%s' "$j" | jq -r --arg src "..." '<same predicate>' 2>/dev/null)" == "true" ]]
```
**Reference:** CWE-754 (improper check for unusual or exceptional conditions); the hook's own fail-closed contract.

### 2. `/chart` does not refuse an autonomous PRD, contrary to its docs and its test

- **HIGH** (confidence: high) `head/.claude/scripts/chart-guard.sh:117-119` — the guard takes the first line of `dec-write-lib.sh context --prd …` as its verdict. That library (unchanged by this PR) prints `unattended` for live signals only and lists the PRD Status line under `--why` as "advisory: a planning-time default for new and decide only". An autonomous PRD therefore yields `interactive`, and the guard prints `interactive` and exits 0.
**File:** `head/.claude/scripts/chart-guard.sh:117`
**Issue:** The guard's header (lines 82-84) and `head/.claude/commands/chart.md:79-80` both list "a PRD whose Status says autonomous" among the refusals, and CD-10 (`head/tests/unit/charting-decisions.bats:146-150`) asserts exit 1. On head, with the br stub on PATH as the suite arranges, CD-10 fails (reproduced: `context --why --prd` prints `interactive` plus `signal: prd prd-status:…`). The same verdict feeds `chart-ticket.sh:407-408` (`close --reason`) and `golden-path.sh` `_gp_is_unattended`.
**Why This Matters:** PRD Appendix E D12 / SDD D-4.3 step 0 is the skill's one hard invariant: a map whose rounds the agent answered is not a map. The shipped behaviour and the shipped documentation disagree, and a test in the PR is red.
**Required Fix:** Decide which contract is right and make the three agree. If the PRD line should refuse: parse `--why` output and refuse on any `signal: prd` line (or add a `--strict` to the lib). If it should stay advisory: drop the claim from the guard header, `chart.md`, and CD-10.

---

## Observations

Non-blocking; medium and low findings, each with the scenario in which it bites.

### Medium

- **MEDIUM** (confidence: high) `head/.claude/scripts/chart-ticket.sh:325` — `resolve` appends `- <name> (<row>, <bead>): <line>` where `<row>` may be `PEND-xxxxxxxx` (accepted by `ROW_RE` at line 46; produced when the ledger writer runs in a linked worktree). `head/.claude/scripts/validate-artifact.sh:1083` requires `DEC-[0-9]{4,}` in every Decisions-so-far bullet, so a map charted from a worktree fails the validator the skill runs at step 10. Reproduced by substituting a PEND id. `resources/REFERENCE.md:74-77` acknowledges PEND rows but not this failure. Either accept `PEND-` in the validator with a WARN, or refuse `resolve` on a PEND row with a pointer to `import`.
- **MEDIUM** (confidence: medium) `head/.claude/skills/discovering-requirements/SKILL.md:77` — the new prototype rule tells the skill to create a `decision:prototype` bead with an open DEC row, but its frontmatter (line 5) grants only `git log` and `wc` under `deny_raw_shell: true`: no `br`, no `dec-write-lib.sh`. No helper exists either (`head/.claude/scripts/beads/create-sprint-task.sh:100-104` refuses type question; `chart-ticket.sh ticket` needs a map). The `defer`/`halt` semantics in `head/.loa.config.yaml.example:143-158` therefore have no mechanical route from the interview that is supposed to trigger them, and `head/tests/unit/unattended-prototype.bats:6` pins prose only. Karpathy: a mechanical behaviour delivered as skill prose. Add a `chart-ticket.sh prototype` (or similar) subcommand and grant it.
- **MEDIUM** (confidence: medium) `head/.claude/commands/plan-and-analyze.md:250-253` — the consumed-map close is written as a slash command (`/chart close <slug> --consumed-by <cycle-id>`) to be run from inside the discovering-requirements skill, which cannot invoke slash commands and whose allowlist has neither `chart-guard.sh` nor `chart-ticket.sh`. This is the single operation the design allows unattended (`chart-guard.sh --close-consumed`); without a route the map stays `handed-off`, keeps counting in `golden_open_maps` (`head/.claude/scripts/golden-path.sh:82`), and the next `/plan` or `/chart` with several maps hits the multi-map rule.
- **MEDIUM** (confidence: medium) `head/.claude/scripts/chart-ticket.sh:459-462` — `research-end` fails the ticket when any file under `.run/` is newer than the dispatch marker. `.run/` is written by hooks and session state throughout a session (dozens of writers under `.claude/hooks` and `lib`), so a compliant, Bash-less research subagent can be failed by writes it did not make. Scope the check to `.beads/`, or to specific `.run/` files the subagent could plausibly touch.

If real beads_rust rejects any of them, every `/chart` session dies at `epic` or at the frontier. Record a one-off run against a real `br` in the PR, or add a `br --help` probe in the suite.

# Sprint 1 Review Feedback

**Reviewer:** Senior Tech Lead Reviewer Agent
**Date:** 2026-10-20
**Sprint Reference:** grimoires/loa/sprint.md
**Implementation Report:** grimoires/loa/a2a/sprint-1/reviewer.md (carries pr/PR.md; no `## AC Verification` section)

---

## Overall Assessment

The change under review is `pr/head.diff`: the `/chart` decision-map workflow (four new scripts, a skill, a command, a research agent), `map` and `spike` artifact types in `validate-artifact.sh`, the SP-1 spike fence and the D-5.9 spike-delete predicate in `block-destructive-bash.sh`, spike handling in `run-mode-ice.sh`, the question-bead lints on the build path, the `charting` planning phase in `golden-path.sh`, and ten bats suites. The shell work is careful: write order and idempotency in `chart-ticket.sh` hold as documented, the unblock probe cleans its worktree on every path, the frontier re-filters `br ready` output, and the fence corpus rows for SP-1 all pass.

I ran the ten touched suites against an overlay of the repository with the PR applied (`pr/head/` over the workspace, executable bits restored). Results:

| Suite | Result |
|---|---|
| charting-decisions | 28/29 — CD-10 fails on head (finding 2) |
| chart-frontier, charting-lint, golden-path-charting, run-mode-ice, unattended-prototype, agents-md-gen | all pass |
| spike-validator | 13/16 — "unparsable ledger keeps the block" fails on head (finding 1); two need `grimoires/loa/spikes/TEMPLATE.md`, absent in this workspace |
| validate-artifact | 48/60 — the 12 failures need the live ledger, absent in this workspace (pre-existing tests) |
| skill-capabilities | 33/36 — the 3 failures are the installed yq (4.40, no `tostring`), pre-existing tests |

Two defects introduced by the PR are reproduced and each is caught by a test the PR itself ships, so the change cannot merge as is. The `reviewer.md` carries only the PR title; there is no `## AC Verification` walkthrough, which is itself an automatic CHANGES_REQUIRED under this skill. Phase 2.5 (adversarial cross-model review) did not run: `.loa.config.yaml` sets `flatline_protocol.code_review.enabled: false`.

**Verdict:** CHANGES REQUIRED

---

## Changes Required

### 1. Safety fence: an unparsable ledger opens the spike-delete gate

- **HIGH** (confidence: high) `head/.claude/hooks/safety/block-destructive-bash.sh:651` — `_fr11_spike_decided` pipes `yq -o=json` into `jq -e`; the hook has no pipefail by design (line 14), so when yq fails to parse `grimoires/loa/decisions.yaml` it prints nothing and jq 1.6 exits 0 on empty input. The predicate then reports "decided" and `git branch -D spike/<slug>` on an unmerged spike branch is allowed.
**File:** `head/.claude/hooks/safety/block-destructive-bash.sh:651`
**Issue:** Reproduced in a scratch repo with `decisions: [unclosed` as the ledger: the hook exits 0 (allow). With no ledger file it blocks (FR-1.1), with a decided row it allows, so the gap is exactly the parse-failure path. The PR's own test "D-5.9: an unparsable ledger keeps the block" (`head/tests/unit/spike-validator.bats:262-269`) fails on head.
**Why This Matters:** The comment at line 641 promises "any failed lookup keeps the block". A corrupted or half-written ledger (the writer uses temp-and-rename, but a hand edit or merge conflict does not) silently turns a fail-closed fence into fail-open, and the lost work is the unmerged prototype the branch exists to preserve.
**Required Fix:** Capture the yq output first and fail closed when it is empty or yq returned non-zero, and do not rely on `jq -e` with possibly empty input:
```bash
local j
j=$(yq -o=json -I0 '.' "$ledger" 2>/dev/null) || return 1
[[ -n "$j" ]] || return 1
[[ "$(printf '%s' "$j" | jq -r --arg src "..." '<same predicate>' 2>/dev/null)" == "true" ]]
```
**Reference:** CWE-754 (improper check for unusual or exceptional conditions); the hook's own fail-closed contract.

### 2. `/chart` does not refuse an autonomous PRD, contrary to its docs and its test

- **HIGH** (confidence: high) `head/.claude/scripts/chart-guard.sh:117-119` — the guard takes the first line of `dec-write-lib.sh context --prd …` as its verdict. That library (unchanged by this PR) prints `unattended` for live signals only and lists the PRD Status line under `--why` as "advisory: a planning-time default for new and decide only". An autonomous PRD therefore yields `interactive`, and the guard prints `interactive` and exits 0.
**File:** `head/.claude/scripts/chart-guard.sh:117`
**Issue:** The guard's header (lines 82-84) and `head/.claude/commands/chart.md:79-80` both list "a PRD whose Status says autonomous" among the refusals, and CD-10 (`head/tests/unit/charting-decisions.bats:146-150`) asserts exit 1. On head, with the br stub on PATH as the suite arranges, CD-10 fails (reproduced: `context --why --prd` prints `interactive` plus `signal: prd prd-status:…`). The same verdict feeds `chart-ticket.sh:407-408` (`close --reason`) and `golden-path.sh` `_gp_is_unattended`.
**Why This Matters:** PRD Appendix E D12 / SDD D-4.3 step 0 is the skill's one hard invariant: a map whose rounds the agent answered is not a map. The shipped behaviour and the shipped documentation disagree, and a test in the PR is red.
**Required Fix:** Decide which contract is right and make the three agree. If the PRD line should refuse: parse `--why` output and refuse on any `signal: prd` line (or add a `--strict` to the lib). If it should stay advisory: drop the claim from the guard header, `chart.md`, and CD-10.

Non-blocking; medium and low findings, each with the scenario in which it bites.

- **MEDIUM** (confidence: high) `head/.claude/scripts/chart-ticket.sh:325` — `resolve` appends `- <name> (<row>, <bead>): <line>` where `<row>` may be `PEND-xxxxxxxx` (accepted by `ROW_RE` at line 46; produced when the ledger writer runs in a linked worktree). `head/.claude/scripts/validate-artifact.sh:1083` requires `DEC-[0-9]{4,}` in every Decisions-so-far bullet, so a map charted from a worktree fails the validator the skill runs at step 10. No helper exists either (`head/.claude/scripts/beads/create-sprint-task.sh:100-104` refuses type question; `chart-ticket.sh ticket` needs a map). The `defer`/`halt` semantics in `head/.loa.config.yaml.example:143-158` therefore have no mechanical route from the interview that is supposed to trigger them, and `head/tests/unit/unattended-prototype.bats:6` pins prose only. # Retrospective Postlude Template

**Version**: 1.0.0
**Purpose**: Embed at END of SKILL.md files for invisible learning extraction

---

## Usage

Copy the `<retrospective_postlude>` section below and paste it at the very END of any skill's SKILL.md file, after all main skill content.

---

## Template

```xml
<retrospective_postlude>
## Invisible Retrospective

After completing main skill logic, scan session for learning opportunities.

**CRITICAL**: This postlude executes SILENTLY. Only surface findings that pass quality gates.

### Step 1: Check Configuration

Read `.loa.config.yaml`:
```yaml
invisible_retrospective:
  enabled: true|false
  skills:
    {current-skill-name}: true|false
```

The effective `enabled` value is the explicit key, else the `loa.profile` default: `.claude/scripts/lib/profile-lib.sh knob invisible_retrospective.enabled true`.

**Exit Conditions** (skip all processing if any are true):
- the effective `invisible_retrospective.enabled` is not `true` → Log action: DISABLED, exit
- `invisible_retrospective.skills.{this-skill}: false` → Log action: DISABLED, exit
- **RECURSION GUARD**: This skill is `continuous-learning` → Exit silently (prevent infinite recursion)
  - INVARIANT: The `continuous-learning` skill MUST NEVER have a retrospective postlude
  - The schema also excludes `continuous-learning` from valid skill values

### Step 2: Scan Session for Learning Signals

Search the current conversation for these patterns:

| Signal | Detection Patterns | Weight |
|--------|-------------------|--------|
| Error Resolution | "error", "failed", "fixed", "resolved", "worked", "the issue was" | 3 |
| Multiple Attempts | "tried", "attempted", "finally", "after several", "on the Nth try" | 3 |
| Unexpected Behavior | "surprisingly", "actually", "turns out", "discovered", "realized" | 2 |
| Workaround Found | "instead", "alternative", "workaround", "bypass", "the trick is" | 2 |
| Pattern Discovery | "pattern", "convention", "always", "never", "this codebase" | 1 |

**Scoring**: Sum weights for each candidate discovery.

**Output**: List of candidate discoveries (max 5 per skill invocation, from config `max_candidates`)

If no candidates found:
- Log action: SKIPPED, candidates_found: 0
- Exit silently

### Step 3: Apply Lightweight Quality Gates

For each candidate, evaluate these 4 gates:

| Gate | Question | PASS Condition |
|------|----------|----------------|
| **Depth** | Required multiple investigation steps? | Not just a lookup - involved debugging, tracing, experimentation |
| **Reusable** | Generalizable beyond this instance? | Applies to similar problems, not hyper-specific to this file |
| **Trigger** | Can describe when to apply? | Clear symptoms or conditions that indicate this learning is relevant |
| **Verified** | Solution confirmed working? | Tested or verified in this session, not theoretical |

**Scoring**: Each gate passed = 1 point. Max score = 4.

**Threshold**: From config `surface_threshold` (default: 3)

### Step 3.5: Sanitize Descriptions (REQUIRED)

**CRITICAL**: Before logging or surfacing ANY candidate, sanitize descriptions to prevent sensitive data leakage.
====
====

Review of sprint-1 is complete. The feedback file is written at `grimoires/loa/a2a/sprint-1/engineer-feedback.md`, ends with the LOA-VERDICT trailer, and `verdict-derive.sh` reports it CONSISTENT.

**Verdict: CHANGES_REQUIRED.** Two defects introduced by the PR were reproduced, and each is caught by a test the PR itself ships:

- **Spike-delete gate fails open on an unparsable ledger.** In `block-destructive-bash.sh`, the new decided-verdict predicate pipes `yq` into `jq -e` in a hook that deliberately has no pipefail. When yq cannot parse the ledger, jq 1.6 sees empty input and exits 0, so `git branch -D spike/<slug>` on an unmerged spike is allowed. The PR's own "unparsable ledger keeps the block" test is red.
- **`/chart` does not refuse an autonomous PRD.** The guard trusts the first line of the ledger writer's `context` verdict, which treats the PRD Status line as advisory only. The guard header, the command doc, and test CD-10 all claim a refusal that does not happen. CD-10 is red on head.

**Non-blocking observations** (five medium, nine low) include: PEND-prefixed row ids written by `resolve` fail the new map validator; the prototype-ticket discipline is prose that the discovering-requirements skill has no tool grants or helper to execute; the unattended map close in `/plan-and-analyze` is specified as a slash command with no mechanical route; `research-end` fails tickets on any `.run/` write during the dispatch; and the `br` flags the new scripts rely on are verified only against a permissive stub.

**How I verified:** I built an overlay of the repository with the PR applied and ran the ten touched bats suites. Seven pass fully. The remaining failures beyond the two above are environmental to this workspace (no spike template, no live ledger, an older yq), and are called out as such in the feedback.

The adversarial cross-model review did not run because `flatline_protocol.code_review.enabled` is false in the config. I also wrote the brief's `review.md` at the repository root in its one-finding-per-line shape, logged the trajectory, and recorded one retrospective learning in NOTES.md about the `jq -e` empty-input hazard.
